facts.text: The user asked to locate matching text between the UDHR and the Cairo Declaration on Human Rights in Islam (CDHRI) and copy/paste it into a middle column.
The user asked for comments in a right-most column about any miss-match between the UDHR left column and the CDHRI middle column.
The user said they would provide the UDHR statements.

The user provided a UDHR statement about disregard and contempt for human rights leading to barbarous acts and the proclamation of freedom of speech and belief and freedom from fear and want as the highest aspiration.
The user provided a UDHR statement labeled Article 10 about the right to a fair and public hearing by an independent and impartial tribunal.
The user provided a UDHR statement labeled Article 11 about the presumption of innocence until proved guilty according to law in a public trial with guarantees for defense.

The user provided a UDHR statement about no one being held guilty of a penal offence for acts or omissions that were not penal offences at the time they were committed, and no heavier penalty than the one applicable at the time.
The user provided a UDHR statement about protection against arbitrary interference with privacy, family, home, or correspondence, and protection against attacks on honour and reputation.
The user provided a UDHR statement about the right to freedom of movement and residence within the borders of each State.
The user provided a UDHR statement about the right to leave any country, including one’s own, and to return to one’s country.
The user provided a UDHR statement about the right to seek and enjoy asylum from persecution in other countries.
The user provided a UDHR statement that the asylum right may not be invoked for prosecutions arising from non-political crimes or acts contrary to the purposes and principles of the United Nations.
